blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Large programmes fail quietly. They almost never die in a single, dramatic moment; instead, they leak time, goodwill and credibility over months, long before anyone is willing to say out loud that the original plan is no longer viable. The best programme leaders treat that slow erosion as the real risk, and organise everything else around spotting and acting on it early.

By the time a traditional red-amber-green report turns red, several earlier signals have usually been missed. Good leaders build informal listening systems to supplement the formal one: weekly quiet conversations with key workstream leads, direct sampling of end users, pointed questions in one-to-ones with the sponsor. These are not substitutes for governance — they are the texture that gives the governance meaning.

No sooner had the original scope been agreed than it began, of course, to change. Skilled programme leaders do not resist that reality; they design for it. They build in regular, scheduled moments of honest renegotiation, where scope, budget, timeline and quality can all be revisited. A programme that never renegotiates is not disciplined — it is in denial.

items.q: According to the text, how do large programmes usually fail?
options: As soon as the scope is agreed
Quietly, leaking time and credibility over months
items.why: "Large programmes fail quietly… they leak time, goodwill and credibility over months."

items.q: What is the purpose of the informal listening systems?
options: To speed up the red-amber-green report
To supplement the formal reporting and catch early signals
To reduce the number of workstreams
items.why: "Good leaders build informal listening systems to supplement the formal one" — para captar sinais antecipados.

items.q: What does the author suggest by saying the RAG report turns red only AFTER signals have been missed?
options: Formal reports are a lagging indicator, not an early warning
items.why: Inferência: o relatório formal fica vermelho tarde demais — ele confirma um problema que sinais mais cedo já mostravam.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Slow erosion is the real risk in large programmes
Scope will inevitably change after it is agreed
A programme that never renegotiates is well disciplined
Informal conversations give governance its meaning
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que nunca renegociar não é disciplina, mas negação — o autor discordaria dessa alternativa.

items.q: The phrase "they are the texture that gives the governance meaning" suggests that…
options: texture is more important than results
formal processes are meaningless without the informal insight behind them
listening systems are a waste of the sponsor's time
items.why: Inferência: sem a escuta informal, a governança formal fica vazia — os sinais reais dão sentido aos números.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver falando sobre o programa que lidera. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, where are we? On paper, all four workstreams are green, the burn rate is within tolerance, and the regulator has raised nothing new this month. If I only read the dashboard, I would tell you we are fine.

But I have spent the last two weeks doing something the dashboard cannot do for me. I sat with each workstream lead for half an hour, no slides, and I sampled a dozen end users directly. And the texture underneath the green is not green. The data migration lead is quietly working weekends to keep her numbers, which tells me the plan is already unrealistic. Two of our sponsors have stopped answering my messages within the day — that is a credibility signal, not a diary problem.

Here is what I am proposing. Next quarter's renegotiation moves forward by three weeks. We put scope, timeline and budget back on the table before the report turns red, not after. I would rather have an uncomfortable conversation now, on our terms, than a crisis one in March.

And to be clear, this is not the programme failing. This is us catching the quiet erosion early enough to still do something about it.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does the dashboard show about the programme this month?
options: All four workstreams are green and the burn rate is within tolerance
The regulator has raised several new concerns
items.why: "all four workstreams are green, the burn rate is within tolerance, and the regulator has raised nothing new."

items.q: What did Oliver do that the dashboard could not do for him?
options: He sat with each lead and sampled end users directly
He escalated the issues to the board
He rewrote the RAG report himself
items.why: "I sat with each workstream lead for half an hour… and I sampled a dozen end users directly."

items.q: Why does Oliver read the data migration lead working weekends as a warning?
options: It signals the regulator is satisfied
It means the budget is too large
It shows the plan is already unrealistic
It proves she is highly committed
items.why: "quietly working weekends to keep her numbers, which tells me the plan is already unrealistic."

items.q: What does Oliver mean by calling the sponsors' slow replies "a credibility signal, not a diary problem"?
options: The delay reflects eroding trust in the programme, not just scheduling
The sponsors want a bigger budget
The sponsors are simply too busy
The messages were sent to the wrong people
items.why: Inferência: ele lê o silêncio como perda de confiança — a quiet erosion — e não como mera agenda cheia.

items.q: How would you best describe Oliver's overall stance?
options: Proactive — renegotiating early to stay in control
Panicked and ready to cancel the programme
Complacent because the dashboard is green
items.why: Inferência: ele antecipa a renegociação para agir cedo, preferindo a conversa difícil agora à crise depois.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Each workstream reports to its own lead but shares the same milestones." A workstream is…
options: a parallel strand of work within a larger programme
items.why: Workstream = frente de trabalho: um ramo paralelo dentro do programa maior.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The programme's ___ is running ahead of plan — we are spending trust faster than money."
items.why: Burn rate = ritmo de gasto; a frase ecoa a ideia de que ele mede também a queima de confiança.

items.q: Benefit realisation is best described as…
options: actually turning a completed programme into the value it promised
the total budget approved by the sponsor
the moment the scope is first agreed
items.why: Benefit realisation = realização de benefícios: o que separa um programa concluído de um bem-sucedido.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "We caught the ___ early — small delays and lost goodwill before any report turned red."
items.why: Quiet erosion = erosão silenciosa: a perda lenta que é o risco real do programa.

items.q: "Strong governance alone was not enough to save the programme." Governance here means…
options: the formal structure of oversight, decision rights and reporting
the office where the team sits
the informal weekly chats with leads
items.why: Governance = governança: a estrutura formal de supervisão e decisão — que precisa da textura informal para ter sentido.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem na gestão de programas complexos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The sponsor still has to sign off on the revised scope." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two workstream leads pushed back on the new timeline." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "None of these cosmetic fixes will move the needle on delivery." This means they will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "We agreed the recovery plan, but the migration team never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — aqui, não levaram.

items.q: "Let's flag the credibility signals to the sponsor before the next review." To flag something means to…
items.why: Flag = sinalizar, chamar atenção para algo antes que vire problema maior.
